questions.question: Which language should the WatchWatcher client use?
questions.rationale: The specification explicitly requires a cross-platform Flutter app, whose implementation language is Dart.

options.label: Dart
options.description: Required by the specified cross-platform Flutter application.

questions.question: Which framework should power the WatchWatcher client?
questions.rationale: Flutter is explicit in the specification.

options.label: Flutter
options.description: Specified cross-platform framework for Android, Linux desktop, and web.

questions.question: Implement the six-module RYA/ASA syllabus, bundled searchable COLREGs reference, dual-standard terminology, threshold-gated adaptive examiner with Gemini JSON evaluation and deterministic offline fallback, local mastery/weak-spot/drill persistence, exact-scale navigation vector visualization, animated Rule 19 encounter visualization, night-light presets, and Android/Linux/web responsive study workflows. Keep all required core study and exam functions available offline.
questions.rationale: Feature scope comes directly from spec.md; Gemini is optional online grading only and must fall back locally.

questions.question: Which managed data stores should the Azure deployment use? Student progress is persisted locally on-device via shared_preferences; the app must remain useful offline.
questions.rationale: The required persistence is local shared_preferences. No server-side sync or Azure dependency is specified, so no Azure datastore is needed.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: No Azure datastore; progress remains in local on-device preferences.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Managed relational database hosted in Azure.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed SQL database hosted in Azure.

options.label: Cosmos DB
options.description: Managed distributed NoSQL database hosted in Azure.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Azure object storage for files and media.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use application features?
questions.rationale: The specification defines local student state but no account or sign-in workflow.

options.label: No
options.description: The offline-first study app has no user account or sign-in requirement.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate to access application API features.
